cards.title: Pull, change, add, commit, push
cards.body: Most days with Git look the same: pull, change files, `git add`, `git commit`, `git push`. Here is the middle of the loop.
cards.code:
git init
echo "hello" > notes.txt
git add notes.txt
git commit -m "Add notes"
git log --oneline

cards.title: Spot the bug
cards.body: GitHub never gets the new file. Which line is in the wrong place?
cards.code:
echo "hello" > notes.txt
git add notes.txt
git push
git commit -m "Add notes"

bug.fix: A push sends commits, and nothing is committed yet. Commit first, then `git push`.

check.question: In the everyday loop, what comes right after editing your files?
check.explanation: Stage your changes first, then commit, then push.

exercise.prompt: You are in your clone of `blog`. Create `post.md` with `echo "# My first post" > post.md`, commit it with the message `Add first post`, and push it to GitHub.
